transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Claire Martinez (Neptune ML Eng), Devon Li (Neptune Platform), Amir Qureshi (Neptune CTO)
Links shared: https://redwood.internal/decks/qprofile-fp8-int8, benchmark spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood/qbench-neptune (note: shared as view link)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles focusing on INT8 vs FP8. Demo of how to push profiles from Console, expected latency/cost tradeoffs, and quality monitoring hooks. Agreed to run a two-week pilot on Dedicated capacity for a Neptune LLM microservice.

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for taking the time. Uh, quick introductions? I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on the account.
[00:07] Claire: Hi Evan, Claire Martinez, ML engineer at Neptune.
[00:09] Devon: Devon Li, I run platform.
[00:11] Amir: Amir Qureshi, CTO.
[00:13] Sanjay: Sanjay Patel, I'm Redwood SE, I'll lead the technical bits today.
[00:18] Evan: Cool. The objective, show the Optimize workflow in the Console and talk through quantization profiles — INT8 and FP8 — and what tradeoffs we've seen in latency and quality. We'll highlight how you can push profiles to Dedicated, and how the monitoring ties in.
[00:32] Claire: Sounds good; our main concern is quality regression. Latency's important but if FP8 breaks generation for our prompts we can't ship.
[00:38] Devon: Also curious about KV cache behavior — does quantization affect cache warming?
[00:42] Sanjay: Short answer: it can. Depending on the kernel and kernel path we take, the KV encoding is compatible, but you may see slightly different cache hit patterns because quantized variants sometimes have different chunking. We'll show logs.
[00:55] Evan: I'm going to share screen — here's the Console, top-level Optimize tab. You can see existing profiles; we have a profile called "neptune-fast-int8" and one called "neptune-balanced-fp8" in the sandbox org.
[01:10] Sanjay: The Console lets you compare profiles side-by-side — token latency, p99, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate, and a small quality delta metric from eval sets. Note the eval delta is a heuristic, we always recommend running your own prompt set.
[01:25] Claire: That heuristic — how is it computed? BLEU? embedding similarity?
[01:29] Sanjay: It's a combination: embedding-based similarity for semantic closeness, plus a reranker model we run on a golden set. It's configurable; you can bring-your-own-eval too. The UI shows a "Quality delta" which is percent relative to baseline FP32.
[01:41] Evan: Let's flip to the perf traces. Here is an INT8 run — same model and sequence length distribution as your sample but with INT8 quantization and our continuous batching on.
[01:52] Sanjay: You'll notice tail latency improvements — p50 drops from ~120ms to ~82ms for short requests, and p95 moves from 420ms to 260ms. Cost per token drops about 28% in this slice.
[02:05] Devon: That's substantial. What's the impact on long-form prompts? Around 2-3k tokens?
[02:09] Sanjay: Long sequences are more mixed. INT8 often benefits throughput, but because kernel selection changes, repetitive attention patterns sometimes see a small quality delta. FP8 tends to maintain better numeric fidelity for long recurrences, but incurs a slight latency penalty — p50 maybe 10-15% higher than INT8.
[02:24] Claire: Can you show me an FP8 trace?
[02:26] Evan: Sure — switching. This FP8 trace shows p50 at ~95ms for short requests, p95 at ~310ms; cost is ~14% lower than FP32 but about 8% higher than the INT8 run. Quality delta shows +0.6% vs baseline on the golden set.
[02:41] Amir: Those deltas — what's a meaningful threshold? Our product folks said they want no more than 1% degradation on core intent extraction tasks.
[02:48] Sanjay: Right, we can set alerts in Optimize that trigger when the quality delta for a profile exceeds your threshold on the prompt set. We also have automatic rollback policies for rollouts.
[02:56] Claire: When you say "rollback" — if a canary on Dedicated fails, does traffic automatically go back to FP32 in Hosted?
[03:02] Sanjay: There are policies — you can fallback to a compatible variant: FP32 hosted, a different quant profile, or a different region. The routing layer will pick the matched model version. We showed a demo of A/B earlier — same idea.
[03:14] Devon: About the KV cache question — can quantized variants share the same cache?
[03:18] Sanjay: Not always. If the runtime uses a different internal representation for KV, caches are isolated. We maintain a compatibility table in the Console. For example some INT8 kernels use the same KV encoding and can reuse cache; FP8 paths often require a different KV serialization. That impacts warm-starts.
[03:32] Claire: Hmm ok — that could affect our latency SLOs for bursty traffic.
[03:35] Evan: For that reason we recommend a short staged rollout: first internal traffic, then 10% external, then full. Also use prefix caching where appropriate.
[03:45] Sanjay: I'm going to run a quick live comparison. I'll trigger two profiles against the same 20 sample prompts from your set. Please note this is demo infra, numbers will vary.
[03:58] [04:00] Sanjay: First run: baseline FP32. Second run: neptune-fast-int8. Third run: neptune-balanced-fp8.
[04:12] [04:20] Sanjay: FP32 p50 118ms, p95 430ms. INT8 p50 76ms p95 270ms. FP8 p50 98ms p95 315ms. Quality pass rate (golden rules): FP32 100%, INT8 96% (misses on two entity-copy cases), FP8 99%.
[04:40] Claire: The entity-copy misses — can you point to an example?
[04:43] Sanjay: Yeah here — prompt 7: "Extract company names and preserve casing." INT8 dropped casing on two tokens in one response. This is subtle but for NER downstream it's important. FP8 preserved casing.
[04:58] Devon: Is that deterministic? Seems like a weird artifact.
[05:01] Sanjay: Not deterministic per-request, more probabilistic under certain kernel math differences — quantization noise creeping into logits for ambiguous tokens.
[05:09] Amir: If we see that in production, what's mitigation? Retrain, or calibration?
[05:14] Sanjay: First step: try out per-channel calibration, and we have targeted bias correction layers, plus you can pin a small subset of layers to FP16 while quantizing the rest. Optimize supports hybrid profiles where layers 0-6 are FP16 and layers 7+ are INT8. That often restores entity fidelity while keeping most of the latency win.
[05:32] Claire: Okay could be a good option. How does console let us build hybrid profiles?
[05:36] Evan: Under Optimize -> Profiles -> Create, choose hybrid and pick layers, or import a JSON profile. You can also run a "quick-scan" which runs a small eval battery and recommends which layers to keep FP16.
[05:47] Claire: Can that quick-scan be run on our Dedicated pilot so numbers match our infra?
[05:51] Sanjay: Yes, the quick-scan can be run in-situ on Dedicated nodes. That is actually the recommended path. We'll need the pilot infra and the prompt set.
[05:59] [06:00] Devon: On Dedicated, we care about instance sizing. INT8 seems to reduce GPU memory — what size recommendations do you have?
[06:06] Sanjay: INT8 reduces memory footprint substantially. For your 7B-ish model, INT8 lets you fit 4 replicas on an A100-80GB when using contiguous KV cache; FP8 you might get 3. For accurate sizing we'll run a pack test during pilot.
[06:19] Evan: I'm going to open the benchmark spreadsheet we linked. You'll see columns: prompt type, seq len, p50, p95, cost delta, quality delta. We highlighted the two failure cases for INT8.
[06:30] Claire: Do you have guardrails so we don't accidentally push a bad profile?
[06:33] Sanjay: Yes — Optimize supports gated rollouts and pre-deployment checks. We also integrate with your CI so your merge pipeline can call the Optimize API to run an eval battery before allowing a profile to be promoted.
[06:45] Amir: Security question — if we run the pilot in our VPC, how does KMS work for key management of model artifacts and telemetry?
[06:52] Evan: For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. Telemetry can be sent to your logging endpoints; the control plane only stores metadata. We'll send the SOC2 and KMS whitepaper after the call.
[07:05] Claire: A practical ask — can you export the exact tokens/outputs for the failed INT8 prompts so our NLU folks can reproduce?
[07:12] Sanjay: Yes we will export raw traces and token-level logits where permitted. For privacy we redact PII. We'll include the raw outputs and the reranker scores.
[07:21] Devon: Ok next steps: pilot on Dedicated for two weeks, run quick-scan and pack test, evaluate hybrid profiles if INT8 shows regression.
[07:29] Evan: Great. Any other questions?
[07:31] Claire: One more — licensing/price delta for Dedicated when using FP8 or INT8? Cost per GPU is the same but effective cost per token changes — do you provide cost modeling?
[07:40] Evan: We provide model-specific cost-per-token guidance in Optimize and the Console shows estimated monthly spend given projected QPS. For pilots we'll provide a custom cost model for your traffic mix.
[07:52] Amir: Sounds good. We're particularly concerned about the entity-copy regression but the hybrid approach sounds promising.
[07:58] Evan: Ok we'll follow up with the FP8/INT8 perf deck and the spreadsheet. We'll propose pilot slots — are mornings next week good for you?
[08:06] Claire: Yes morning PST is best.
[08:08] Devon: Works for platform.
[08:10] Amir: Good.
[08:12] Evan: Thanks everyone. We'll circle back with action items.

Meeting wrap / quick recap:
- Demo of Console Optimize comparing INT8 and FP8 profiles.
- Observations: INT8 best for short-latency and cost, FP8 better numeric fidelity for long recurrences and entity preservation.
- Recommended path: two-week Dedicated pilot, run quick-scan + pack test, try hybrid profile if entity regressions occur.

References/shared artifacts:
- FP8 vs INT8 perf deck: https://redwood.internal/decks/qprofile-fp8-int8
- Benchmark sheet (demo runs): https://sheets.redwood/qbench-neptune
- SOC2/KMS notes (to send): https://redwood.internal/compliance/soc2-kms.pdf

End of transcript.
